title: Whispers of the Morning
summary: A lyrical exploration of dawn's quiet arrival, capturing the sensory beauty of light, sound, and awakening through poetic prose.

pages.text: The sky grew soft before the sun. Shadows turned from deep navy blue to pale lavender. A single bird called out, brave and loud. Its song seemed to draw the light forward.
pages.scene: A misty landscape transitioning from night to early dawn

pages.text: Then came the first ray of golden light, touching the ground like a gentle hand. It crept across the dewy grass, each blade catching fire. The cold air grew warm.
pages.scene: Morning light spreading across wet grass and wildflowers

pages.text: All around, the world awoke. Flowers opened their faces to the new day. The dew drops turned to tiny mirrors, reflecting the growing brightness.
pages.scene: Close-up of flowers with dewdrops, unfurling petals

pages.text: The bird sang louder now, joined by many voices. Their song rose like a cloud into the brightening sky. It was the sound of joy, the sound of beginning.
pages.scene: Multiple birds in trees, silhouetted against the expanding light

pages.text: Slowly, slowly, the night gave way. The sky turned from purple to pink to gold to blue. The change seemed both loud and silent at once.
pages.scene: Gradient sky showing the full spectrum of sunrise colors

pages.text: Everything was new, yet everything was the same. The grass had not changed its shape. The flowers did not grow. But the light transformed it all into something wonderful and strange.
pages.scene: Familiar landscape completely transformed by morning light

pages.text: This moment would not last. Soon the day would rush in with all its noise and speed. But now, in these few precious moments, the world was calm and beautiful.
pages.scene: The quiet magic of early morning, peaceful and contemplative

pages.text: The sun climbed higher. The show was nearly done. Yet those who paused to see it would carry this beauty with them. They would know: the world begins again each morning, if we only look.
pages.scene: Full sunrise with a figure standing in contemplation, looking outward
